title: Hof deployment plan (v2, target-bound)
description: hofctl plan's v2 output contract - everything plan-v1 already has (baseline/desired/drift/summary/operations/warnings/blockers, unchanged in shape) plus exact target binding, planning policy, image verification policy per image.verify operation, and the bootstrap-only recovery/suppliedTls fields delivery item 8's apply needs. plan-v1 stays the historical, unchanged contract - this is an addition, not a breaking replacement. See ADR 0004.

planId.description: sha256 of the plan's own inputs+baseline+target binding, deterministic - never includes a timestamp. Unlike plan-v1, this also covers `target` (host, port, user, the exact accepted host-key fingerprint) and `policy`/`recovery`/`suppliedTls` - a host-key change, a different baseline generation, or a different recovery recipient all produce a different planId, exactly as ADR 0004 requires ("a host-key change invalidates the plan").

executable.description: false when blockers is non-empty - apply must refuse a plan that isn't executable.

target.description: Exactly which target this plan was computed against - apply's own stale-plan recheck re-derives this under the lock and refuses to proceed if it no longer matches.

hostKeySha256.description: The exact accepted SSH host-key fingerprint from the same connection this plan's own inspection used - never the caller-supplied trust anchor alone, and never a value inspectTarget() merely hoped was accepted. Required (non-null) in ssh mode; always null in local mode (there is no SSH transport to fingerprint).

installationId.description: bootstrap: a fixed, deterministic placeholder (never a real installation id - see plan-command.mjs's BOOTSTRAP_INSTALLATION_ID_PLACEHOLDER). applied: the real installation id this baseline was resolved from.

baselineGeneration.description: The baseline's own generation this plan was diffed from (0 for a synthetic bootstrap baseline) - apply's stale-plan recheck compares this against a fresh baseline read under the lock.

policy.description: The planning-time choices this specific plan was computed with - apply must never silently apply a different policy than the one the operator actually approved.

recovery.description: Required for a bootstrap plan (never for applied) - the external age recipient secrets.sops.yaml is encrypted to in addition to the target's own operator key, so a lost target host doesn't also mean permanently lost secrets. Never itself a secret - a public age recipient is safe to record in a plan.

suppliedTls.description: Present only when the manifest's tls.mode is "supplied" - the sha256 of the certificate file as read from the operator's own workstation at planning time (never the certificate or key content itself, and never the private key's digest either - only enough to let apply detect the file changing between planning and execution).

operationId.description: A three-digit sequence prefix (this plan's own execution order) plus a descriptive suffix - unlike volume/service identifiers, operation ids legitimately start with a digit.

units.description: Keyed by hof.unit (the actual Compose service key), not by catalog artifact - Wachter's API and its agent share one artifact but are two units, and collapsing them loses one entirely.

configFingerprint.description: sha256 of this unit's own full rendered Compose service definition (image, environment, labels, volumes, ...) - catches a domain/CORS/browserPush/TLS-driven env change even when the image itself didn't change.

schemaVersion.description: Present only for a service with a catalog database entry - the release lock's declared schema version for its database component (from/to, see the catalog schema).

baselineState.description: The last-applied state this plan is diffing from - either loaded from /var/lib/hof/state, or the synthetic empty baseline (mode: bootstrap, generation: 0, installationId: null) on a truly clean host.

topologyDigest.description: sha256 over the rendered topology, backup config, and Caddyfile together - the one field that catches a change (like a backup schedule edit) with no per-unit Compose footprint at all.

desiredState.description: What services.yml + the catalog + the release lock render to right now - a plain snapshot, not itself a generation.

imageTrust.description: Only for image.verify - exactly how apply must verify this specific image, carried in the plan itself so apply never has to re-consult the release lock at execution time to know whether an image needs a real Cosign identity check or is trusted by digest pin alone (a third-party image with no Hof-controlled signing identity - see release-lock-v1.schema.json's own thirdParty/trust split).

condition.description: Only for readiness.wait - what actually counts as ready for this specific unit. Most units have a real Compose healthcheck and must reach "healthy"; the gateway deliberately has none (see render-topology.mjs's own comment on why), so it only ever waits for "running".

argv.description: Only for database.migrate - the catalog's own database.command for this component, so an approved plan is self-sufficient and apply never has to re-interpret the catalog to know what to run.

volume.description: Only for database.migrate/backup.create - the catalog's own database.volume (or the volume backup.create is protecting).
